title: Remove Duplicates From an Unsorted Linked List
summary: Given the head of a linked list, identify all values that appear more than once, then remove the nodes containing these values.
statement: Given the head of a linked list, identify all values that appear more than once, then remove the nodes containing these values. Return the modified linked list.
constraints: Remove every node whose value occurs more than once anywhere in the unsorted list.
Preserve the original relative order of values occurring exactly once.
reference_solution:
def remove_all_duplicate_values(head):
 from collections import Counter
 counts=Counter();node=head
 while node:counts[node.val]+=1;node=node.next
 dummy=ListNode(0,head);previous=dummy;node=head
 while node:
  if counts[node.val]>1:previous.next=node.next
  else:previous=node
  node=node.next
 return dummy.next

hints: First learn global value frequencies; a one-pass local check cannot know future duplicates.
Count values, then traverse again behind a dummy node.
Unlink a node when its count exceeds one; otherwise advance the retained-tail pointer.
Every node is removed exactly when its globally counted value is duplicated, and the pointer rewiring preserves all unique nodes in order.
